The '''Open Technology Fund''' ('''OTF''') is an American nonprofit corporation<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.opentech.fund/news/a-new-independent-otf/|title=A New, Independent OTF|website=Open Technology Fund|language=en|access-date=2024-08-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200717202610/https://www.opentech.fund/news/new-independent-otf/ |archive-date=2020-07-17}}</ref> that aims to support global [[Internet freedom]] technologies. Its mission is to "support open technologies and communities that increase free expression, circumvent [[censorship]], and obstruct repressive [[surveillance]] as a way to promote [[human rights]] and open societies."<ref name="values-principles">{{cite web|url=https://www.opentech.fund/about/values-principles/|title=Values & Principles|website=Open Technology Fund|access-date=20 October 2019}}</ref> Until its formation as an independent entity, the Open Technology Fund had operated as a program of [[Radio Free Asia]].<ref name=":0" /> As of November 2019, the Open Technology Fund became an independent nonprofit corporation and a grantee of the [[U.S. Agency for Global Media]].<ref name=":0" /> On March 14, 2025, [[Donald Trump|President Trump]] issued an [[executive order]] that directed that the [[U.S. Agency for Global Media]] be eliminated "to the maximum extent consistent with applicable law", along with several other agencies.<ref name=":4">{{cite web |date=March 14, 2025 |title=Continued Reduction of the Federal Bureaucracy |url=https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/03/continuing-the-reduction-of-the-federal-bureaucracy/ |publisher=The White House |access-date=2025-03-16}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bianco |first=Ali |date=2025-03-15 |title=Trump's next agency cuts include US-backed global media, library and museum grants |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/03/15/donald-trump-agency-cuts-00232119 |access-date=2025-03-16 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Pager |first=Tyler |date=2025-03-15 |title=Trump Orders Gutting of 7 Agencies, Including Voice of America's Parent |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/03/15/us/politics/trump-order-voice-of-america.html |access-date=2025-03-16 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

==History==
The Open Technology Fund was started in 2012 by [[Libby Liu]], then president of [[Radio Free Asia]] (RFA), as a pilot program within RFA to help better protect reporters and sources for the news organization with enhanced digital security technology.<ref name="Paletta 2016">{{cite news |last1=Paletta |first1=Damian |title=How the U.S. Fights Encryption--and Also Helps Develop It; Agencies are developing encryption tools for secure communications, even as the FBI battles for access to an encrypted iPhone |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=February 22, 2016}} {{ProQuest|1766924876}}</ref><ref name="otf-history"/><ref name=":0" /> Under U.S. Secretary of State [[Hillary Clinton]], the [[United States Department of State|State Department]] adopted a policy of supporting global internet freedom initiatives.<ref name="Lake-2015-09-18"/> At this time, RFA began looking into technologies that helped their audiences avoid censorship and surveillance.<ref name="Lake-2015-09-18" /> Journalist [[Eli Lake]] argued that Clinton's policy was "heavily influenced by the [[Internet activism]] that helped organize the [[2009 Iranian presidential election protests|green revolution in Iran in 2009]] and other [[Arab Spring|revolutions in the Arab world in 2010 and 2011]]".<ref name="Lake-2015-09-18">{{cite web|last1=Lake|first1=Eli|title=Government Is Fighting Itself on Encryption|url=https://www.bloombergview.com/articles/2015-09-18/government-is-fighting-itself-on-encryption|website=Bloomberg View|publisher=Bloomberg L.P.|type=Column|access-date=15 February 2016|date=18 September 2015}} Note: The author uses "Open Whisper" when referring to [[Open Whisper Systems]].</ref>

In September 2014, the OTF worked with [[Google]] and [[Dropbox (service)|Dropbox]] to create an organization called Simply Secure to help improve the usability of privacy tools.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Rushe|first1=Dominic|title=Google and Dropbox launch Simply Secure to improve online security|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2014/sep/18/google-dropbox-simply-secure-security-tech|website=The Guardian|access-date=14 February 2016|date=18 September 2014}}</ref> 

In March 2017, the OTF's future was reported as under question due to the Trump administration's unclear positions on Internet freedom issues.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Melendez|first1=Steven|title=U.S.-Backed Efforts To Promote Openness And Democracy Are At Risk In The Age Of Trump|url=https://www.fastcompany.com/3068328/us-backed-efforts-to-promote-openness-and-democracy-are-at-risk-in-the-age-of-trump|website=Fast Company|publisher=Fast Company, Inc|date=24 March 2017}}</ref> However, the OTF continued to receive Congressional funding under the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]].

In November 2019, OTF announced it had become an independent nonprofit corporation.<ref name=":0"/> The OTF has funded digital privacy and security technology, including [[The Tor Project]], [[Signal (messaging app)|Signal]],<ref name="Verma 2020">{{cite news |last1=Verma |first1=Pranshu |title=Lawsuit Argues Dismissal of Government-Funded Media Employees Was Unlawful |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/23/us/politics/michael-pack-global-media.html |access-date=31 October 2023 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=24 June 2020}}</ref> and other [[encryption]] projects.<ref name="Paletta 2016">{{cite news |last1=Paletta |first1=Damian |title=How the U.S. Fights Encryption--and Also Helps Develop It; Agencies are developing encryption tools for secure communications, even as the FBI battles for access to an encrypted iPhone |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=February 22, 2016}} {{ProQuest|1766924876}}</ref>

In June 2020, Libby Liu resigned as CEO of OTF (see {{Section link||Dispute over board}}).<ref>{{Cite news|last=Wong|first=Edward|date=2020-06-15|title=V.O.A. Directors Resign After Bannon Ally Takes Charge of U.S. Media Agency|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/15/us/politics/voice-of-american-resignations.html|access-date=2020-06-17|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Cox|first=Joseph|date=2020-06-17|title=CEO of Open Technology Fund Resigns After Closed-Source Lobbying Effort|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/open-technology-fund-ceo-resigns/|access-date=2020-06-17|website=Vice|language=en}}</ref>

On March 14, 2025, President Donald Trump issued an executive order directing federal agencies to reduce their functions "to the maximum extent consistent with applicable law," including the [[U.S. Agency for Global Media]] (USAGM),<ref name=":4" /> which disburses congressionally approved funding to OTF. The following day, USAGM senior advisor Kari Lake announced the termination of the OTF's federal grant, stating that the "award no longer effectuates agency priorities."<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Adragna |first=Anthony |date=21 March 2025 |title=Open Technology Fund sues to release blocked grant |url=https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2025/03/open-technology-fund-sues-to-release-blocked-grant-00242305 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250424150017/https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2025/03/open-technology-fund-sues-to-release-blocked-grant-00242305 |archive-date=24 April 2025 |access-date=1 November 2025 |website=Politico}}</ref>

In response, OTF filed suit against USAGM seeking the release of congressionally appropriated funds.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Claburn |first=Thomas |date=25 March 2025 |title=OTF, which backs Tor, Let's Encrypt and more, sues to save its funding from Trump cuts |url=https://www.theregister.com/2025/03/25/otf_tor_lets_encrypt_funding_lawsuit/ |access-date=1 November 2025 |website=The Register}}</ref> In its court filings, OTF argued that the termination would prevent an estimated 45 million users living under authoritarian regimes from accessing tools that enable uncensored access to the Internet and secure communications. The organization further claimed that, as the largest funder in the space, "the vast majority of internet freedom technology projects anywhere in the world will cease and the internet freedom technology field as whole will be largely decimated."<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 March 2025 |title=Civil Action No. 1:25-cv-840 |url=https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.dcd.278630/gov.uscourts.dcd.278630.1.0.pdf |access-date=1 November 2025 |website=CourtListener}}</ref>

The decision drew bipartisan concern from members of Congress who described OTF's work as vital to U.S. foreign policy priorities and Internet openness.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Verma |first=Pranshu |date=20 March 2025 |title=Trump ends program millions in China use for internet, worrying Congress |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2025/03/20/trump-ends-internet-access-china-iran-otf/ |access-date=1 November 2025 |website=Washington Post}}</ref><ref name=":2" /> Although Lake later stated that she had withdrawn the letter rescinding OTF's funding,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adragna |first=Anthony |date=27 March 2025 |title=Trump administration reverses funding block on Open Technology Fund |url=https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2025/03/trump-administration-reverses-funding-block-on-open-technology-fund-00253854 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250331174350/https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2025/03/trump-administration-reverses-funding-block-on-open-technology-fund-00253854 |archive-date=31 March 2025 |access-date=1 November 2025 |website=Politico}}</ref> USAGM reportedly was sending payments after April 3.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adragna |first=Anthony |date=13 June 2025 |title=Open Technology Fund says it’s owed $2M |url=https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2025/06/open-technology-fund-says-its-owed-2m-00405827 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250712001400/https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2025/06/open-technology-fund-says-its-owed-2m-00405827 |archive-date=12 July 2025 |access-date=1 November 2025 |website=Politico}}</ref> In June, a federal judge ordered USAGM to release OTF's fiscal year 2024 funds.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adragna |first=Anthony |date=20 June 2025 |title=Federal judge orders funding for Open Technology Fund |url=https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2025/06/federal-judge-open-technology-fund-must-be-funded-through-fiscal-year-00415770 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250620204921/https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2025/06/federal-judge-open-technology-fund-must-be-funded-through-fiscal-year-00415770 |archive-date=20 June 2025 |access-date=1 November 2025 |website=Politico}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Adragna |first=Anthony |date=14 October 2025 |title=Open Technology Fund says Trump administration is |access-date=1 November 2025 |website=Politico}}</ref> In late October, OTF petitioned the court to compel the agency to disburse overdue fiscal year 2025 funding.<ref name=":3" />

==Organization and funding==

Initial funding was allocated in 2011 from Congress to the [[Broadcasting Board of Governors]], which then provided $7 million to [[Radio Free Asia]].<ref name="Paletta 2016"/> The Open Technology Fund operated for seven years as a program of Radio Free Asia, a U.S. government-funded, nonprofit international corporation that provides news, information and commentary in East Asia. Since 2019, the OTF has had its own Board of Directors and receives its funding directly from the [[U.S. Agency for Global Media]] (USAGM), an independent agency of the U.S. government.<ref name="otf-history">{{cite web |title=OTF's History |url=https://www.opentech.fund/about/our-history/ |website=Open Technology Fund |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230825091156/https://www.opentech.fund/about/our-history/ |archive-date=August 25, 2023 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The OTF is sustained by annual grants from the USAGM, which originate from yearly U.S. Congressional appropriations for State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs.<ref name="otf-history"/> According to the OTF, it works with other publicly funded programs to fulfill a U.S. Congressional mandate to sustain and increase global [[freedom of information]] on the Internet with public funds.<ref name="otf-history"/>

==Projects==
The OTF funds third-party [[Information technology security audit|audits]] for all the [[source code|code]]-related projects it supports.<ref name="code-audits"/> It has also offered to fund audits of "non-OTF supported projects that are in use by individuals and organizations under threat of censorship/surveillance".<ref name="code-audits"/> Notable projects whose audits the OTF has sponsored include [[Cryptocat]],<ref>{{cite web|first1=Alban|last1=Diquet|first2=David|last2=Thiel|first3=Scott|last3=Stender|title=Open Technology Fund CryptoCat iOS Application Penetration Test|url=https://isecpartners.github.io/publications/iSEC_Cryptocat_iOS.pdf|publisher=iSEC Partners|access-date=13 February 2016|date=7 February 2014}}</ref> [[Commotion Wireless]],<ref name="isecpartners-2013"/> [[TextSecure]],<ref name="isecpartners-2013">{{cite web|title=Working with the Open Technology Fund |url=https://isecpartners.github.io/2013/10/14/open-tech-fund-report-release.html |first1=Tom |last1=Ritter |publisher=iSEC Partners |date=14 October 2013 |access-date=13 February 2016}}</ref> [[GlobaLeaks]],<ref name="isecpartners-2013"/> [[MediaWiki]],<ref>{{cite web|last1=Steipp|first1=Chris|title=Improving the security of our users on Wikimedia sites|url=https://blog.wikimedia.org/2015/04/20/improving-security-for-our-users/|website=Wikimedia Blog|publisher=Wikimedia Foundation|access-date=13 February 2016|date=20 April 2015}}</ref> OpenPGP.js,<ref>{{cite web|last1=Heiderich|first1=Mario|last2=Kotowicz|first2=Krzysztof|last3=Magazinius|first3=Jonas|last4=Antesberger|first4=Franz|title=Pentest-Report OpenPGP.js 02.2014|url=https://cure53.de/pentest-report_openpgpjs.pdf|publisher=Cure53|access-date=14 February 2016|date=February 2014}}</ref> [[Nitrokey]],<ref>{{Cite web|last1=McDevitt|first1=Dan|title = Nitrokey Storage Firmware and Hardware Security Audits|url = https://www.opentech.fund/article/nitrokey-storage-firmware-and-hardware-security-audits|publisher = Open Technology Fund|access-date =15 February 2016|date=2 October 2015}}</ref> [[Ricochet (software)|Ricochet]]<ref>{{cite web|last1=Cox|first1=Joseph|title='Ricochet', the Messenger That Beats Metadata, Passes Security Audit|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/ricochet-encrypted-messenger-tackles-metadata-problem-head-on/|website=Motherboard|publisher=Vice Media LLC|access-date=17 February 2016|date=17 February 2016}}</ref> and [[Signal (messaging app)|Signal]].<ref name=time-20200626/> The OTF also matched donations to the auditing of [[TrueCrypt]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=White|first1=Kenneth|last2=Green|first2=Matthew|title=IsTrueCryptAuditedYet?|url=http://istruecryptauditedyet.com/|website=Open Crypto Audit Project|access-date=14 February 2016|date=21 January 2014}}</ref> In 2014, the OTF reported that it had funded more than 30 technology code audits over the past three years, identifying 185 privacy and security vulnerabilities in both OTF and non-OTF-funded projects.<ref name="code-audits">{{cite web|last1=Hurley|first1=Chad|title=Code Audits are Good. Making Code Audits Public is Better|url=https://www.opentech.fund/article/code-audits-are-good-making-code-audits-public-better|website=Open Technology Fund|access-date=14 February 2016|date=10 December 2014}}</ref>

In 2015, [[The Tor Project]] announced that OTF would sponsor a [[bug bounty program]] coordinated by [[HackerOne]].<ref name="tor-bounty">{{cite web|last1=Cox|first1=Joseph|title=The Tor Project Is Starting a Bug Bounty Program|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/the-tor-project-is-starting-a-bug-bounty-program/|website=Motherboard|publisher=Vice Media LLC|access-date=14 February 2016|date=29 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Conditt|first1=Jessica|title=Tor plans to launch a bug bounty program|url=https://www.engadget.com/2015/12/31/tor-plans-to-launch-a-bug-bounty-program/|website=Engadget|publisher=AOL Inc.|access-date=14 February 2016|date=31 December 2015}}</ref> The program was initially invite-only and focuses on finding vulnerabilities that are specific to The Tor Project's applications.<ref name="tor-bounty"/>

In October 2019, OTF Technology Director Sarah Aoun discussed the findings of OTF-funded research into a Chinese government mobile application, telling [[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] that the app essentially amounts to a "surveillance device in your pocket."<ref name="Thorbecke-2019">{{cite web|url=https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/news/story/chinas-popular-education-app-surveillance-device-pocket-advocacy-66262334|title=China's popular education app is a 'surveillance device in your pocket,' advocacy group says|last1=Thorbecke|first1=Catherine|date=18 October 2019|website=Good Morning America}}</ref> "The access itself is significant", OTF Research Director Adam Lynn told ''[[The Washington Post]]''. "The fact that they've gone to these lengths [to hide it] only further heightens the scrutiny around this."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/asia_pacific/chinese-app-on-xis-ideology-allows-data-access-to-100-million-users-phones-report-says/2019/10/11/2d53bbae-eb4d-11e9-bafb-da248f8d5734_story.html|title=Chinese app on Xi's ideology allows data access to 100 million users' phones, report says|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|last=Fifield|first=Anna|date=12 October 2019}}</ref>

According to its funding agency, the U.S. Agency for Global Media, OTF's impact by 2019 was global, with over 2 billion people using OTF-supported technology daily, and more than two-thirds of all mobile users having OTF-incubated technology on their devices.<ref name=USAGM-OTF2019>{{cite web|url=https://www.usagm.gov/networks/otf/|title=Open Technology Fund|website=USAGM|access-date=30 December 2019}}</ref> "As authoritarian states worldwide increasingly attempt to control what their citizens read, write, and even share online," said OTF CEO Libby Liu, "this next stage in OTF's growth could not come at a more crucial time."<ref name=USAGM2019-11-25/>

OTF had $2 million of funding from the USAGM to assist with the [[2019–20 Hong Kong protests]], but this funding was frozen by USAGM CEO Michael Pack in June 2020 as China was preparing to introduce a new [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|national security law for Hong Kong]].<ref name=time-20200626>{{cite news |url=https://time.com/5860163/trump-hong-kong-funding-freeze/?amp=true |title=Trump Administration Freezes Funds Intended to Benefit Hong Kong Protesters |last=Perrigo |first=Billy |publisher=Time |date=26 June 2020 |access-date=5 July 2020}}</ref><ref name=scmp-20200703>{{cite news |url=https://www.scmp.com/comment/opinion/article/3091438/us-has-been-exposed-funding-last-years-hong-kong-protests |title=US has been exposed for funding last year's Hong Kong protests |last=Lo |first=Alex | website = [[South China Morning Post]] |date=3 July 2020 |access-date=5 July 2020}}</ref>

== Dispute over board ==
On June 17, 2020, the newly appointed head of USAGM, [[Michael Pack]], fired the board of OTF and CEO [[Libby Liu]].<ref>{{Cite web|author=Jennifer Hansler and Brian Stelter|title='Wednesday night massacre' as Trump appointee takes over at global media agency|url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/17/media/us-agency-for-global-media-michael-pack/index.html|access-date=2020-10-18|website=CNN|date=17 June 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2020-06-19 |title=Trump-backed US global media agency chief under fire for purge |url=https://www.dw.com/en/trump-backed-us-global-media-agency-chief-under-fire-for-purge/a-53870348 |access-date=2020-10-17 |website=Deutsche Welle |language=en-GB}}</ref> Liu had already tendered her resignation on June 13, 2020, effective July 13, 2020, on a separate issue regarding the usage of closed-source software.<ref name=":1" /> The new board was named, consisting of Jonathan Alexandre (Senior Counsel, [[Liberty Counsel|Liberty Counsel Action]]), Robert Bowes (Senior Advisor to the Secretary, U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development), Bethany Kozma (Deputy Chief of Staff, United States Agency for International Development), Rachel Semmel (Communications Director, Office of Management and Budget), Emily Newman (Chief of Staff, USAGM), and Pack as chairman.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Open Tech. Fund v. Pack, 470 F. Supp. 3d 8 {{!}} Casetext Search + Citator |url=https://casetext.com/case/open-tech-fund-v-pack |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220331044419/https://casetext.com/case/open-tech-fund-v-pack |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 31, 2022 |access-date=2022-06-16 |website=casetext}}</ref> The next day, the board fired president Laura Cunningham.

On June 23, 2020, District of Columbia attorney general [[Karl A. Racine]] filed suit under the District's Nonprofit Corporations Act to reverse Pack's replacement of the OTF board.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Verma|first=Pranshu|date=2020-06-23|title=Lawsuit Argues Dismissal of Government-Funded Media Employees Was Unlawful|language=en-US|work= [[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/23/us/politics/michael-pack-global-media.html|access-date=2020-10-17|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=AG Racine Files Lawsuit to Resolve Presence of Dueling Boards at District Nonprofit Open Technology Fund |url=https://oag.dc.gov/release/ag-racine-files-lawsuit-resolve-presence-dueling |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121064657/https://oag.dc.gov/release/ag-racine-files-lawsuit-resolve-presence-dueling |archive-date=January 21, 2021 |access-date=January 18, 2021 |website=oag.dc.gov |publisher=Office of the Attorney General of the District of Columbia}}</ref> The lawsuit alleged that the actions violated the "firewall" clause in federal communications regulations that shield government news agencies from political interference. 

On July 21, 2020, the [[U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia]] blocked the findings in an emergency stay, warning that these actions could endanger the work of activists against Internet censorship in countries with repressive government.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Hsu|first=Spencer S.|title=Appeals court blocks Trump administration takeover of organization fighting digital censorship and surveillance|language=en-US|newspaper=Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/legal-issues/appeals-court-blocks-trump-administration-takeover-of-organization-fighting-digital-censorship-and-surveillance/2020/07/21/4f4299c4-cb5d-11ea-bc6a-6841b28d9093_story.html|access-date=2020-10-17|issn=0190-8286}}</ref> On October 16, 2020, in a separate case, the [[DC Superior Court]] ruled that the changes were unlawful, reinstated the previous board, and ruled that any changes the new board made were invalid.<ref>{{Cite web|title=DC Court Rules in Dispute Over Open Technology Fund Board|url=https://www.voanews.com/a/usa_dc-court-rules-dispute-over-open-technology-fund-board/6197239.html|access-date=2020-10-17|website=Voice of America|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Summary Judgment DC v Pack|url=https://oag.dc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-10/OTF-Summary-Judgment.pdf|website=Office of the Attorney General for the District of Columbia}}</ref>

Beginning in August 2020, OTF came under increasing pressure from Pack and USAGM leadership. According to Axios,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Allen-Ebrahamian |first1=Bethany |title=In media agency shakeup, conservative groups push for Falun Gong-backed internet tools |url=https://www.axios.com/falun-gong-us-agency-global-media-001fcf52-95fa-43de-b0c7-0cd7cfc2918f.html |access-date=18 January 2021 |publisher=Axios.com |date=23 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Sewell |first1=Tia |title=Trump's War on the U.S. Agency for Global Media |url=https://www.lawfaremedia.org/article/trumps-war-us-agency-global-media |access-date=18 January 2021 |publisher=Lawfare |date=12 January 2021}}</ref> this was related to OTF's reluctance to extend grants to [[Falun Gong]]-related enterprises working on technology directed against China's [[Great Firewall]]; the ''New York Times'' noted Falun Gong and its ''[[Epoch Times]]'' media group often supported the Trump administration.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Roose |first1=Kevin |title=Epoch Times, Punished by Facebook, Gets a New Megaphone on YouTube |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/02/05/technology/epoch-times-youtube.html |access-date=18 January 2021 |work=New York Times |date=5 February 2020}}</ref> On August 18, USAGM announced it was setting up its own Office of Internet Freedom with less strict grant requirements and began soliciting OTF's grantees to apply to the new office.<ref>{{cite web |title=CEO Pack revives USAGM's Office of Internet Freedom; agency funds internet firewall circumvention technologies |url=https://www.usagm.gov/2020/08/18/ceo-pack-revives-usagms-office-of-internet-freedom-agency-funds-internet-firewall-circumvention-technologies/ |website=www.usagm.gov |publisher=US Agency for Global Media |access-date=18 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Fischer |first1=Sara |title=Scoop: USAGM soliciting OTF partners as it withholds funds |url=https://www.axios.com/usagm-soliciting-otf-partners-as-it-withholds-funds-e59fa0d1-5ec9-4fcc-a5c1-64176fa23644.html |access-date=18 January 2021 |publisher=Axios.com |date=13 October 2020}}</ref> On August 20, OTF sued USAGM in the U.S. Court for Federal Claims for withholding nearly $20 million in previously agreed grants.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fischer |first1=Sara |title=Scoop: Open Technology Fund sues administration for $20M in missing funds |url=https://www.axios.com/scoop-open-technology-fund-sues-administration-for-20m-in-missing-funds-90b5420d-2f41-4e50-b58b-6a517af26cd6.html |access-date=18 January 2021 |publisher=Axios.com |date=20 August 2020}}</ref>

On October 15, [[summary judgment]] was granted nullifying Pack's attempt to replace the OTF board.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AG Racine Wins Lawsuit Resolving Leadership Crisis at District Nonprofit Caused by Trump Appointee |url=https://oag.dc.gov/release/ag-racine-wins-lawsuit-resolving-leadership-crisis |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112192042/https://oag.dc.gov/release/ag-racine-wins-lawsuit-resolving-leadership-crisis |archive-date=January 12, 2021 |access-date=January 18, 2021 |website=oag.dc.gov |publisher=Office of the Attorney General of the District of Columbia}}</ref>

In June 2020, OTF had asked law firm [[McGuireWoods]], which had been advising it pro bono, for help in its conflict with the USAGM and Pack. McGuireWoods said it could not help in the case. OTF learned in December 2020 that the reason was that McGuireWoods had decided to investigate OTF on behalf of USAGM and Pack instead.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Folkenflik |first1=David |title='I Was Speechless': Law Firm Investigated Its Own Ex-Client For Trump VOA Chief |url=https://www.npr.org/2021/03/10/974122042/i-was-speechless-law-firm-investigated-its-own-ex-client-for-trump-voa-chief |access-date=20 March 2021 |publisher=National Public Radio |date=10 March 2021}}</ref> The [[Government Accountability Project]], citing records obtained via the [[Freedom of Information Act (United States)|Freedom of Information Act]], claimed McGuireWoods had billed USAGM $1.625 million at an average rate of $320 an hour after receiving a no-bid contract to investigate OTF as well as [[Voice of America]] employees.<ref>{{cite web |title=Press Release: Whistleblowers Reveal More Alarming Details About Law Firm Contracts Awarded by Voice of America Overseer to Investigate Federal Employees |url=https://whistleblower.org/press-release/press-release-whistleblowers-reveal-more-alarming-details-about-law-firm-contracts-awarded-by-voice-of-america-overseer-to-investigate-federal-employees/ |website=whistleblower.org |date=18 March 2021 |publisher=Government Accountability Project |access-date=20 March 2021}}</ref>
